findings.observation: The public source definition is a mutable global registry with a flat Settings dictionary; registration overwrites by name and no immutable host-scoped policy plan exists.

Readiness classifies schema failures from lower-cased exception message text, reflects for Execute while the instruction contract exposes ExecuteAsync, and can replay the user operation after provider dispatch.

Direct untyped queries collapse rows to dictionaries, so duplicate names are overwritten; typed projection serializes each dictionary to JSON and deserializes it per row. Only record count is bounded.
ProjectionResolver uses a process-global unbounded Type cache, reflects only flat public scalar properties, and exposes relational Column naming as the physical abstraction.
The public coordinator says commits across adapters atomically while implementation explicitly performs best-effort sequential commits and cannot roll back already committed adapters.
The family announces full filter handling while query and count scan records into memory; bounded candidate scanning is separate, and a batch can execute add/update/delete bulk calls sequentially.
DataCaps has query/write/isolation tokens but no source policy, neutral inspection/result, mapping-plan, registered-operation, completion-reason, or effect/result/lane contracts.

DeleteAll may fall back from Clear instruction after NotSupportedException, batches defer mutation loads, raw queries are separate paths, and none can enforce a source read-only policy that does not exist.
Current exception and telemetry paths interpolate native message text or high-cardinality entity identifiers; exact provider failure typing and public redaction are not shared contracts.

Exact declaration scan finds no Data.Source, StorageLifecycle, ReadLanes, RecordSet, OperationPlan, or MappingPlan contract. Existing Query/Scalar names belong to older repository/direct surfaces rather than the registered-operation grammar.
